gaps.sentence: She apologized for the ___ caused by the delay (CONVENIENT).
gaps.hint: negative noun needed — the delay was a bad thing
gaps.explanation: A delay causes inconvenience (negative prefix in- + noun); the sentence needs the noun, not the adjectives.

gaps.sentence: There are many ___ (SIMILAR) between the two languages.
gaps.explanation: 'Many' needs a plural countable noun: similarities (note the -ty to -ties spelling).

gaps.sentence: Her suitcase was ___ , so the airline charged extra (WEIGHT).
gaps.hint: weighing too much — that is why she paid extra (over-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means too much: overweight explains the extra charge.

gaps.sentence: It is ___ to smoke inside public buildings (LEGAL).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: against the law (il-)
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'legal' is 'illegal' (il- before l). An adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: He lost his job because of his ___ (HONESTY).
gaps.hint: negative noun needed — he lost his job
gaps.explanation: Losing a job implies wrongdoing, so the negative noun 'dishonesty' (dis- + honesty) is needed.

gaps.sentence: This guidebook is really ___ for travellers (USE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ful means full of: useful. 'Useless' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ to accept the conditions at first (WILLING).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: she did not want to
gaps.explanation: 'At first' suggests reluctance, so the negative adjective 'unwilling' (un- + willing) is needed.

gaps.sentence: The meeting has been ___ until Thursday (SCHEDULE).
gaps.hint: arranged for a new time (re-); past participle needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again/afresh: rescheduled means given a new time. The passive needs the past participle.
